chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Yunus ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I have a neighbor from Quraysh, from the family of Muhriz, who has publicized my name and made me well-known; whenever I passed by him, he would say: This is the Rafidi, who carries the wealth to Ja'far ibn Muhammad.'

He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'So supplicate to Allah against him when you are in the night prayer, while you are prostrating in the final prostration of the first two cycles. So praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and glorify Him, and say:'

O Allah, so-and-so son of so-and-so has publicized me and made me well-known, and angered me and exposed me to hardships. O Allah, strike him with an immediate arrow that occupies him with it from me. O Allah, bring closer his death and cut off his trace, and hasten that, O Lord, this moment, this moment.

He said: 'So when we arrived in Kufa, we arrived at night, and I asked my family about him. I said: What happened to so-and-so? They said: He is sick. And the end of my speech had not passed until I heard a cry from his house, and they said that he had died.'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific method and timing for supplicating against an enemy or mocker according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia practice of *du'a al-dhar'* (supplication against an enemy) using a specific, potent formula recited in the final prostration of the first two rak'ahs of night prayer. The immediate fulfillment of the prayer upon the companion's return to Kufa serves as a narrative validation of the supplication's efficacy, a theme frequently cited by scholars to demonstrate the spiritual authority of the Imams. It highlights the social tension of the era, where public labeling as 'Rafidi' was a significant form of social and political marginalization.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Malik Bin Atiyya, from Yunus Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws: ‘There is a neighbour of mine from Qureysh from the family of Muhriz, who has noted my name and publicises me every time I pass by him saying, ‘This is the Rafizi (rejector). He carries the wealth to Ja’far Bin Muhammadasws’ (instead of the ruling authorities)’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So heasws said to me: ‘So supplicate to Allahazwj against him when you were in the night Salat, while you are prostrating during the last Sajdah from the first two Cycles. So Praise Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic and Glorify Himazwj and said,

‘O Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>! So and so, son of so and so has publicised me and is being aggressive with me, and has angered me and exposed me to the harrassment. O Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>! Strike him with an arrow immediately for him to be too pre-occupied with it from me. O Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>! And Draw closer his death, and Cut-off his traces, and Hasten that, O Lord<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, this moment, this moment!’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So when we proceded to Al Kufa, we arrived at night, and I asked our family members about him. I said, ‘What happenned to so and so?’ So they said, ‘He is sick’. So the end of my speech had not passed until I heard a shriek from his house, and they said that he had died’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Malik ibn ‘Atiyyah from Yunus ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Once I said to abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘I have a neighbor from Quraysh from the family of Muhriz who propagates against me negatively.

Whenever I pass by he calls me a Rafida (rejecting successors to the Holy Prophet who are not special members of his family) and that I collect funds for Ja’far ibn Muhammad, recipient of divine supreme covenant.’
The Imam said, ‘Pray to Allah against him in the last Sajdah (prostration) of the second Rak’at of Tahajjud (nightly prayer).

Praise Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, and glorify Him and say, ‘O Lord, so and so, son of so and so propagates against me negatively, he has caused me anger and has exposed me to danger, O Lord, strike him a quick arrow to divert him away from me, O Lord, bring the time of his death closer, eliminate his traces and make it fast, O Lord, in this hour, in this hour!’

When I arrived in al-Kufa during the night and asked my family about him, how is so and so doing? They told me that he was ill. My words were not finished when I heard crying from the house of that man. They said that he had died.”’
